messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: beta derivatives
parts:
I used Wolfram Alpha to calculate the log probabilty
function back on the unconstrained parameters:

http://www.wolframalpha.com/share/clip?f=d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427eemsglp0d6v

There's a rather nasty term in the denominator that
quickly goes to zero.

unconstrained: y = logit(x)
constrained: x = inv_logit(y)

p(x) = beta(x|0.8,0.8) o= x^(-0.2) * (1-x)^(-0.2)

p(y) = p(x) * |dx/dy|

|dx/dy| = inv_logit(y) * (1 - inv_logi(y))

The full probability function back on the unconstrained
value is pretty easy:

log p(y) = log(inv_logit(y)^1.2 * (1 - inv_logit(y)^1.2))

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] beta derivatives
parts:
That looks nastier than it should. Here's my derivation:

log p(x) = (a-1)*log(x) + (b-1)*log(1-x) + c
dx/dy = -x*(1-x)
log p(y) = a*log(x) + b*log(1-x) + c
(c = -logΓ(a) - logΓ(b) + logΓ(a+b).)

then

dlog p(y) / dy
= dlog p(y) / dx * dx / dy
= -(a/x - b/(1-x)) * x*(1-x)
= -a*(1-x) + b*x
= -a*(1-inv_logit(y)) + b*inv_logit(y).

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] beta derivatives
parts:
On 10/25/12 6:11 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> That looks nastier than it should. Here's my derivation:
>
> log p(x) = (a-1)*log(x) + (b-1)*log(1-x) + c

Grr. Argh.

I messed up right here by using (1-a) instead
of (a-1). This isn't helping my prior of being
right on future derivations!

> dx/dy = -x*(1-x)
> log p(y) = a*log(x) + b*log(1-x) + c
> (c = -logΓ(a) - logΓ(b) + logΓ(a+b).)
>
> then
>
> dlog p(y) / dy
> = dlog p(y) / dx * dx / dy
> = -(a/x - b/(1-x)) * x*(1-x)

This is how Stan actually computes it,
because we just apply the chain rule. This
is problematic as x -> 0 or x -> 1.

If we transform the scale of the variate to

logit_beta_log(y|a,b) = log p(y),

we could write:

parameters {
real y;
}
transformed parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> x;
x <- inv_logit(y);
}
model {
y ~ logit_beta(a,b);
}

and everything's copacetic because Matt's derivation
has a pleasantly behaved gradient on y:

I haven't thought through what happens to the gradients
of a and b, though.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] beta derivatives
parts:
On Thursday, October 25, 2012 7:51:26 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I haven't thought through what happens to the gradients
of a and b, though.

Matt brought it up on the thread about limiting cases. If either a or b approaches zero but not both, I think it's not valid. If both a and b approach zero, the beta converges to a Bernoulli, but the probability parameter depends on the relative rates at which a and b approach zero, which is hard for Stan to know.

Ben
